sheetsIndicative.note: one worksheet ('callsigns'): header Value,Status,Type,Reserved to Date,Original Start Date,Licence Type then 146,763 data rows. Status vocabulary Allocated (96,222), Reserved (50,250), Available (281) and blank (10); Type is 'Call Sign - Amateur' on every row. Licence Type carries the product vocabulary (Full 53,886, Foundation 28,595, Intermediate 12,057, Club 1,644, Temporary Reciprocal 37) with 50,544 blank. Original Start Date populated on 96,161 rows (1903-05-03 to 2021-01-29); Reserved to Date populated on 112 rows (2021-02-02 to 2023-01-07).

raw-extract-sheet-1-callsigns.csv.contentsIndicative: mechanical extract of the single sheet; header Value,Status,Type,Reserved to Date,Original Start Date,Licence Type then 146,763 rows. Anomalies preserved verbatim: one Value is empty (blank call sign, Reserved); one is literally ',,' (two commas, Reserved); 'G6 FMU' has an interior space; three Values carry a trailing non-breaking space (G0TQK, G7IWE, 2E1HON); two are lower-case (g0jrk, 2e1GTD); 472 four-character call signs (two-letter-suffix heritage series) and 87 call signs of six to nine characters, most of them reciprocal 'M/...' forms including curiosities such as M/#PT2FM, M/#YO3IES and M/EI-8-DJ. Dates arrive typed and are rendered ISO (date-only; no time-of-day components).

normalised--sheet-1-callsigns.csv.contentsIndicative: header callsign,status,licence_class,reserved_to_date,original_start_date; 146,763 rows sorted by callsign (source order carries no meaning - not callsign-sorted, dates not monotonic). Status carried verbatim (10 blanks preserved); licence_class carries the source product vocabulary verbatim (50,544 blanks); reserved_to_date and original_start_date carried as ISO from the typed workbook. The constant Type column is required-present but not carried. Three trailing non-breaking spaces were trimmed from callsigns (counted in the converter notes, never silent); the empty Value, the ',,' Value and the interior-space 'G6 FMU' are preserved verbatim. The empty callsign sorts first, then ',,'.
